title: Which cities nearly doubled, and how do we reach Mumbai from Patna?
description: The table of Indian cities is used to find the cities whose population nearly doubled between two thousand one and two thousand eleven, and the number that takes Patna close to Mumbai. Keeko then raises a hand, thinking Ahmedabad also nearly doubled.
teaching_notes: One idea: to test for doubling, double the earlier number and see whether it is close to the later number; to compare two populations, find the multiplier by trying whole numbers. Ask the class to double Bengaluru's earlier number before the check is shown. Watch for students who call a city doubled because it grew by a large amount.

source: Are there cities whose population has almost doubled? Which are they?
By what number should we multiply Patna's population to get a number close to that of Mumbai?
video_script.why: The child can round populations to the nearest lakh and subtract, and now doubles and multiplies them to compare cities.
video_script.substitution: Double the 2001 number to the nearest lakh and compare it with the 2011 number; to compare Patna with Mumbai, try whole-number multipliers on Patna's lakhs.
video_script.anchor: The table of Indian cities with columns for 2011 and 2001, and two questions printed above it.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko sees that Ahmedabad grew by about 20 lakh, like Surat, and says Ahmedabad also nearly doubled. Ahmedabad had about 35 lakh, twice that is 70 lakh, but it has only about 56 lakh.

final_answer.value: Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Surat and Vadodara nearly doubled; multiply Patna's population by about 7.39
final_answer.spoken: Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Surat and Vadodara nearly doubled, and we multiply the population of Patna by about seven point three nine

never_show: the exact multiplier before the answer beat
maths_rules: to the nearest lakh: Bengaluru 43 to 84, Hyderabad 36 to 68, Surat 24 to 45, Vadodara 17 to 36
double of the 2001 number: 86, 72, 48 and 34 lakh, each close to the 2011 number
Ahmedabad: 35 lakh doubled is 70 lakh, but 2011 is about 56 lakh, so not close
Patna about 17 lakh, Mumbai about 124 lakh: 7 × 17 = 119, 8 × 17 = 136, so about 7
video_script.design: One idea: double the earlier number and compare, then find a multiplier by trial. Wrong idea: Keeko says a big rise means doubling. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.
open_questions: The book lists Pimpri-Chinchwad but its two columns are jumbled in the extracted text; the video does not rely on that row.
